title: 8.4 A 4GHz, 0.69%-Accuracy Voltage-Droop Detector with Multiple Remote Sensing and Under 2-Cycle Detection Latency in 2nm GAAFET
problem: Voltage droop detection in modern SoCs requires both PVT-tolerant direct sensing and remote-capable distributed detection; previous digital detectors (TDC-based) suffer from PVT sensitivity and low conversion gain; analog detectors have bulky blocks, limited integration, and routing/frequency constraints.
motivation: Per-core voltage scaling to minimize power consumption is critical in modern SoCs but requires accurate, fast droop detection to prevent supply violations.
method: 2nm GAAFET droop detector with compact distributed remote droop detectors (RDD) sampling at up to 4GHz, synchronized by a PVT-tolerant main droop detection controller (DDC), achieving <2-cycle latency with 0.69% accuracy.
key_novelty: Distributed remote droop detectors with centralized PVT-tolerant control enabling high-frequency sampling without routing constraints.
contributions: PVT-tolerant centralized control without analog blocks
primary_theme: Fast distributed voltage droop detection for per-core power scaling
